### Security · Rate limits

Group key: `security.rateLimit`

Max requests per client, per scope, within the rate-limit window. Changes apply live.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `windowMin` — Window (minutes) | `number` | `15` | — | The period every limit below is counted over. Changing it restarts the current window, so in-flight counters reset to zero. |
| `global` — Global (req / window / client) | `number` | `1000` | — | — |
| `auth` — Auth endpoints | `number` | `20` | — | Every /api/auth call together. The per-kind limits (emails, SMS, sign-ins…) are auth.rateLimits. |
| `restRead` — REST read (GET) | `number` | `300` | — | — |
| `restWrite` — REST write (POST/PATCH/DELETE) | `number` | `120` | — | — |
| `edge` — Edge function invokes | `number` | `60` | — | — |

All six apply live. The window used to be the exception — `express-rate-limit` reads
`windowMs` once at construction — so the limiters are rebuilt when it changes. Saving the
group **without** changing the window does not rebuild, so a no-op save cannot hand every
throttled caller a fresh allowance.

### Security · Rate-limit rules

Group key: `security.rateLimitRules`

Custom rules on top of the built-in scopes. Every matching rule applies and the most restrictive wins; rules can only tighten limits. Changes apply live.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rules` — Rules (JSON array) | `json` | — | — | Match by method / path glob / role; bucket by ip, user, apiKey, role or global. |

### Auth · Attack protection

Group key: `auth.attackProtection`

CAPTCHA on the auth endpoints and on any other route you choose, and a leaked-password check.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `captchaEnabled` — Enable CAPTCHA protection | `bool` | `false` | — | Clients must then send a token in the x-captcha-response header on every guarded call, auth calls included (fetchOptions.headers with client.auth). |
| `captchaProvider` — CAPTCHA provider | `select` | `hcaptcha` | — | One of `hcaptcha`, `turnstile`. |
| `captchaSecret` — CAPTCHA secret | `password` | — | yes | — |
| `captchaSiteKey` — Site key (hCaptcha, optional) | `text` | — | — | When set, hCaptcha also checks the token was issued for this site key. |
| `captchaAuthEndpoints` — Guarded auth endpoints | `json` | `["/sign-up/email","/sign-in/email","/sign-in/anonymous","/sign-in/magic-link","/email-otp/send-verification-otp","/email-otp/request-password-reset","/phone-number/send-otp","/request-password-reset"]` | — | Which auth calls need a token. Any of /sign-up/email, /sign-in/email, /sign-in/anonymous, /sign-in/magic-link, /email-otp/send-verification-otp, /email-otp/request-password-reset, /phone-number/send-otp, /request-password-reset. All of them by default, as in Supabase. |
| `captchaRoutes` — Other guarded routes | `json` | `[]` | — | Any other route: a table's REST API (/rest/v1/<table>), an edge function (/api/edge/<name>), storage. * matches any run of characters. No methods means every method. Server-side callers must send a token too. |
| `leakedPasswordProtection` — Prevent use of leaked passwords | `bool` | `false` | — | Rejects passwords found in HaveIBeenPwned. Only the first 5 characters of the SHA-1 hash are sent. |

### Auth · SSO (OIDC / SAML)

Group key: `auth.sso`

The single switch for OIDC / SAML SSO, including per-organization SSO. When on, it mounts the SSO plugin and its /api/auth/sso/* endpoints. When off, no provider can be registered or used. The provider a user reaches is tenant data in ssoProvider records, not an organization setting here.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` — Enabled | `bool` | `false` | — | Required for all SSO, including per-organization SSO. Auth · Organizations has no SSO switch of its own. |

### Auth · Organizations

Group key: `auth.organization`

End-user organizations (Better Auth organization plugin): creation, teams, and member limits. SSO is not configured here. Enable it in Auth · SSO, the only switch that governs SSO.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` — Enabled | `bool` | `true` | — | — |
| `allowUserToCreateOrganization` — Users can create orgs | `bool` | `true` | — | — |
| `teamsEnabled` — Teams inside organizations | `bool` | `false` | — | Adds Better Auth team sub-groups and their endpoints. This is unrelated to SSO; org admins register identity providers at runtime. |
| `maxMembers` — Maximum members per organization | `number` | `0` | — | 0 = unlimited. Applies when a member is added directly, when an invitation is accepted, and when SSO auto-provisions a member. |

### Storage · Policies

Group key: `storage.policies`

Authorize storage with PostgreSQL row level security instead of the built-in owner rule.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` — Use RLS policies for storage | `bool` | `false` | — | When on, every read and write is decided by the policies on storage.files, the same way table access is. The migration installs policies reproducing the built-in behaviour, so turning this on changes nothing until you write your own. When off, the built-in rule applies: an object is readable if it is public or if you own it. |

Off by default because turning it on changes who can read every object in the project, and
an upgrade does not get to do that silently. The migration installs policies reproducing the
built-in behaviour, so switching over changes nothing until you write your own.

### Logs · History and retention

Group key: `logs.retention`

Keep log lines in the database so the Logs screen can look further back than the in-memory buffer and survive a restart. Retention is applied by the data-retention job.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` — Store logs in the database | `bool` | `true` | — | Off keeps the in-memory buffer only: history is capped by CONSOLE_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE and lost on restart. |
| `retentionDays` — Keep logs for (days) | `number` | `7` | — | Lines older than this are deleted on the next data-retention run. |
| `maxRows` — Maximum stored lines | `number` | `2000000` | — | Hard ceiling regardless of age; the oldest lines above it are deleted. 0 disables the cap. |

### Realtime · Retention

Group key: `realtime.retention`

Prune processed realtime outbox rows. Only completed/failed (terminal) rows are removed; pending and processing rows are never touched.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` — Enabled | `bool` | `true` | — | — |
| `completedDays` — Keep delivered events (days) | `number` | `7` | — | Completed realtime events, and messages sent with realtime.send, older than this are purged. |
| `failedDays` — Keep failed events (days) | `number` | `30` | — | Failed realtime events are kept longer for debugging. |

What the Studio SQL editor may run. Changes apply to the next query.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allowWrites` — Allow writes from the SQL editor | `bool` | `true` | — | On, the editor runs anything, as the database owner. Off, every statement runs in a Postgres READ ONLY transaction and INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and DDL are refused. |

### API · REST

Group key: `api.rest`

Limits for the auto-generated REST API. Changes apply on the next request.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `maxRows` — Max rows per request | `number` | `1000` | — | Upper bound on rows a single GET returns. The parser also enforces a hard ceiling of 1000. |
| `rpcSecurityDefiner` — Exposed SECURITY DEFINER functions | `text` | `""` | — | Comma-separated function names reachable over /rest/v1/rpc/. A SECURITY DEFINER function runs as its owner and bypasses the caller's row-level security, so each one must be listed here explicitly. Empty means none are exposed. |

Function names are stored verbatim: they are matched against `pg_proc.proname`, and a quoted
`CREATE FUNCTION "MyFn"` really is stored as `MyFn`, so case is not folded. Entries longer
than Postgres' 63-byte identifier limit, or carrying control characters, are rejected on save.

### API · Keys

Group key: `api.keys`

Whether a project API key is required to reach the REST API.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `requireApiKey` — Require a project API key | `bool` | `false` | — | When on, every REST request must carry a valid publishable or secret key in the apikey header. Off by default so an app running against an older version keeps working across an upgrade. Turn it on once your clients send the key: revoking a key then cuts that caller off without touching a single policy. |

Off by default so an app running against an older version keeps working across an upgrade.
Turn it on once your clients send the key: revoking a key then cuts that caller off without
touching a single policy. The keys themselves are not settings — they live in their own table
and are managed from Project Settings → API keys or `motherbase keys`.

### AI assistant

Group key: `ai.assistant`

Bring your own model key. The assistant runs server side and can only do what your account can do.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` — Enabled | `bool` | `false` | — | — |
| `provider` — Provider | `select` | `anthropic` | — | One of `anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini`, `deepseek`, `qwen`, `glm`, `moonshot`, `mistral`, `xai`, `groq`, `openrouter`, `compatible`. |
| `model` — Model | `text` | — | — | Any model id the provider accepts. Leave blank to use the provider default. |
| `apiKey` — API key | `password` | — | yes | — |
| `baseUrl` — Base URL | `text` | — | — | Leave blank to use the provider's own endpoint. Required for a custom OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM). |
| `maxSteps` — Maximum tool steps per message | `number` | `12` | — | — |
| `autoApproveWrites` — Run write actions without confirmation | `bool` | `false` | — | Off by default. When off, the assistant proposes changes and you press Run. |

### Git · GitHub

Group key: `git.github`

A GitHub OAuth App (Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps). Its Authorization callback URL must be exactly the callback URL below.

| Field | Type | Default | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clientId` — Client ID | `text` | — | — | — |
| `clientSecret` — Client secret | `password` | — | yes | — |
| `callbackUrl` — Authorization callback URL | `text` | — | — | The Studio page GitHub returns the browser to. Its origin is also where the push webhook is delivered. |
